brief: A shelf unit rated to hold 50 kg of books, with two drawers.

requirements.evidence: Full bases at levels 0–1 (piece:0,0,* and 1,0,*) plus a half-base column, topped with covers cover:-1,1,1, cover:0,0,1 and cover:1,0,1. A row of books (prop:2) and a stack of books (prop:1) sit on the top and are visible.
drawer:0#-1,1#cut and drawer:1#-1,1#cut sit on the cut faces of the stacked half bases at (-1,1), levels 0 and 1.

The configurator checks fit and collisions only. It knows nothing about load or strength, or about the material you print in. Nothing here shows the unit can hold 50 kg. Load-test it yourself before you trust it with a heavy book load.

finish.summary: I built a two-storey shelf unit three cells wide with two drawers. The configurator checks fit and collisions only, so it can't rate the unit for 50 kg or any other load. The build is 61 parts, about 2.9 kg of filament and roughly 71 hours of printing. At the bottom are full bases at (0,0) and (1,0). The drawers need half bases, and a half base can only sit on another half base, so they are in a stacked half-base column at (-1,1). The top of storey 2 is closed with covers to make the shelf surface. capOpenFaces put end caps on all open faces, so the bays are closed and books go on the top. lockJoints bolted the joints. I staged a row of books and a stack of books on top. check_build passes with no issues and meshClash reads clear.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
